new_statements.quote: [p.57] Cette règle s'applique dans toutes les positions d'un énoncé sauf la pénultième. Celle-ci est prosodiquement marquée dans la mesure où le noyau vocalique se trouvant dans cette position fait l'objet d'un allongement phonétique automatique. C'est uniquement ici qu'un ton modulé haut descendant peut apparaître. [fn.2: Il s'agit d'une règle postlexicale.] [p.134] En Vi la voyelle préfixale subit en isolation ainsi qu'en fin de groupe prosodique un allongement. Il s'agit d'une règle post-lexicale plus généralement rencontrée dans les langues bantoues et qui consiste à allonger le noyau de la syllabe se trouvant en position de pénultième. Cette voyelle devient donc particulièrement saillante à l'instar de la voyelle radicale des thèmes dissyllabiques.
new_statements.translation: [p.57] This rule [one tone per syllable nucleus] applies in every position of an utterance except the penultimate. The latter is prosodically marked in that the vowel nucleus in this position undergoes automatic phonetic lengthening. Only here can a falling high-low contour tone appear. [fn.2: This is a post-lexical rule.] [p.134] In Vi(ya) the prefix vowel [of CV-CV nouns] undergoes lengthening in isolation and at the end of a prosodic group. This is a post-lexical rule found more generally in Bantu languages, which lengthens the nucleus of the syllable in penultimate position. That vowel thus becomes particularly salient, like the root vowel of disyllabic stems.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Geviya is a tone language (underlying /H/, /L/ and toneless morphemes; rightward H spread; phonological word = tone domain) with no lexical/contrastive stress; the only prominence is on the penultimate syllable of the utterance / prosodic group (hence the word penult in citation forms), realised as automatic post-lexical vowel lengthening (mora insertion), the sole position licensing a falling HL contour; utterance-final H tones are lowered. Van der Veen treats this penultimate lengthening as the language's accentual property (pp.121-122: Geviya and Getsogo accentually similar to Sesotho-type penultimate length-accent) and notes (2001 fn.6) that it is the penult, not the root syllable, that is marked.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; root vowel of disyllabic stems said to be salient (and in B30 generally root vowels are longer), but no secondary accent is posited.
new_statements.exceptions: Lengthening/HL licensing is tied to utterance- or prosodic-group-penultimate position, not every word; non-integrated loanwords are realised with a H tone on the penultimate (1991 sec.8); the 1991/1992 papers had left open whether the penult was intonationally marked, resolved in 1999/2001 as post-lexical penultimate lengthening.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the utterance / prosodic group (post-lexical): penultimate syllable before pause; in isolation (citation forms) this is the word's penultimate syllable. Tone itself is lexical with the phonological word as domain.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe ge-viya (ɣe-βiya) as spoken by the Eviya in the single village (quarters Mavono/Mokaba/Byogo) on the right bank of the Ngounie opposite Fougamou = Glottolog eviy1235 / ISO gev ('Vi' in Van der Veen 2003). No dialect split. Van der Veen notes heavy B40 (Eshira) lexical influence but B30 grammar/phonology. The published 2003 chapter text is held by the project under another language's folder (here1253/).
